data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves are clearly attached at the same node, visible in close-up images, with 5-6 leaves per node)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are arranged in tight groups at each node along the stem, with no long internodes between leaf clusters)

B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade without divisions into leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A

C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (margins are smooth without teeth or serrations; some damage is visible but not natural toothed margin)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (longer than wide, tapering to a point at apex, broadest near base)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tapers to a sharp point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (base is broadly rounded, not tapered or heart-shaped)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein runs length of leaf with secondary veins branching off and curving toward margin)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible, numerous, closely spaced, arching toward margin (secondary veins are prominent, parallel to each other, and form a distinct network)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny, glabrous (surface is smooth and glossy, reflecting light; no visible hairs)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or fuzz on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is short, leaf blade appears to attach directly to stem)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petiole is round in cross-section, not flattened or winged)

D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (stem is green, soft, and flexible, not woody)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem surface)
    19. Stem color: green (stem is bright green, with some brownish coloration at nodes)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (surface is smooth without ridges or lenticels)

E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no structures resembling stipules visible at leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no exudate visible when stem is damaged or cut)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint at leaf base; not applicable as leaf complexity is simple)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no modified stems or leaves functioning as tendrils)

F. Notes: Multiple leaves show holes and margin damage, likely from physical or biological factors; damage is not uniform across leaves. The plant exhibits a whorled leaf arrangement with 5-6 leaves per node. All images show the same individual seedling from slightly different angles. The pink tag is an artificial marker and not a plant feature. No flowers or fruits are visible.
